title: Online matrimonial fraud - a rising category of cybercrime
p1:
The person you trust the most online may not always be who they claim to be.

A growing number of cybercrime cases now begin with a simple conversation on a matrimonial platform.
p2:
Many people believe matrimonial fraud only happens when someone asks for money directly. The reality is more deceptive.

Fraudsters often spend weeks or months building emotional trust before creating a fake emergency, investment opportunity, or financial request. This method is known as a romance scam, where emotions become the tool for manipulation.
p3:
The biggest warning sign is not always the request for money. It is the pattern behind it — avoiding video calls, sharing inconsistent personal details, rushing commitment, or creating repeated financial problems.

A simple verification step can prevent major losses: verify identity independently, avoid sharing sensitive information, and never make financial decisions based only on an online relationship.
conclusion: Have you or someone you know encountered suspicious behavior on matrimonial platforms? What verification steps do you think everyone should follow?
